promotion_evidence: data-prototype (HarryPotter2/Unreal), macOS arm64, CoreText provider: `ctest --test-dir out/macos-arm64 -R '^(native_typography_contracts|canvas_compatibility_contracts)$' --output-on-failure` -> 2/2 passed (0.08 s); shaping, ligature/combining/RTL cluster handling, font fallback, and the NativeText=False bitmap-compatibility cursor contract all hold

data-prototype, macOS arm64: `python3 Build/smoke_maps.py --renderer=xopengl --maps=PrivetDr --output=out/macos-arm64/Testing/HP2/_gatecheck/Artifacts/gatecheck-smoke-maps.json` -> 1/1 maps passed; engine log records `XOpenGL: native text backend ready (text.ready)` and reaches `Entering main loop.` with no script/native/package/render/assert/critical marker

the default is reached without any opt-in: `UClient::StaticConstructor` sets `NativeText = 1` (`HarryPotter2/Unreal/Engine/Src/UnCamMgr.cpp`), and the launcher model defaults `settings.nativeText = true` (`HarryPotter2/Unreal/SDLLaunch/Src/HP2LauncherModel.h`), so an absent `[Display] NativeText` key resolves to enabled in both the engine and the launcher UI
retail profile: NOT verified. No data-retail launch of this configuration has been run, so `retail-verified` is not claimed
platform coverage: macOS arm64 / CoreText only. The Linux arm64 FreeType provider compiles but has not been run with the default on

browser build: unaffected either way. `web-wasm64` sets `HP2_DISABLE_NATIVE_TEXT_BACKEND=ON` and compiles `HP2_HAS_NATIVE_TEXT_BACKEND=0`, so no text provider exists in the wasm module and the gate cannot change what the page renders
bitmap-font compatibility mode is unchanged and remains selectable: `[Display] NativeText=False` in Game.ini, the launcher's toggle, or `UClient::StaticConstructor` at build time

wasm (Emscripten) provider added: same FreeType/HarfBuzz sources as Linux, with a small seam that reads the game's own System/Simyou.ttf out of the module filesystem for FT_New_Memory_Face (there is no fontconfig and no page-side font download)

wasm evidence so far is limited to: web_boot_smoke passes and the engine logs 'XOpenGL: native text backend ready (text.ready)'. Small-HUD legibility in the browser has NOT been reviewed by eye, so this provider is not runtime-verified
WebAssembly uses MEMORY64; the seam's EM_ASM bridges need setValue for out-parameters and Number() for pointer arguments
Emscripten's FS.readFile returns a Uint8Array for a raw read; asking for encoding 'binary' yields an array whose charCodeAt is undefined, which silently zeroed every byte of the font
